title: Portrait of Galileo Galilei
creator: Justus Sustermans
why_public_domain: Painting from 1636; the artist died in 1681. A faithful photo of a 2-D artwork made before 1929 is public domain. OpenStax prints it without a rights credit.
original_holder: Uffizi Galleries, Florence (painting); image file from OpenStax Astronomy 2e
caption: Galileo at about 72, painted by Justus Sustermans in 1636. He holds a telescope, the instrument that made his name.

title: Portrait of Galileo (engraving after Sustermans)
creator: Unknown engraver, after Justus Sustermans
why_public_domain: Printed in 1893 in a book by Oliver Lodge, who died in 1940. Published before 1929, and the engraver is anonymous.
original_holder: Oliver Lodge, Pioneers of Science (London: Macmillan, 1893), via Project Gutenberg #28613 (Fig. 52)
caption: An engraving of Galileo in old age, based on the Sustermans portrait. Its message was simple: the man with the telescope.

title: Jupiter's satellites, 7-13 January 1610, as Galileo recorded them
creator: After Galileo Galilei's Sidereus Nuncius (1610); redrawn for Oliver Lodge
why_public_domain: Redraws observations Galileo published in 1610. This version was printed in 1893, before 1929.
original_holder: Oliver Lodge, Pioneers of Science (London: Macmillan, 1893), via Project Gutenberg #28613 (Fig. 44)
caption: Six nights in January 1610: a few small "stars" shift position around Jupiter from night to night. Galileo saw that they were moons circling another world.

title: Early telescopic drawings of Saturn by different observers
creator: Compiled after drawings by Galileo and later 17th-century observers; printed for Oliver Lodge
why_public_domain: The original drawings are 17th century, and this plate was printed in 1893. Published before 1929.
original_holder: Oliver Lodge, Pioneers of Science (London: Macmillan, 1893), via Project Gutenberg #28613 (Fig. 46)
caption: Thirteen guesses at one planet. The first is Galileo's: Saturn with two companions at its sides. Better lenses later showed that it was a ring.

title: Captain Cook's vessel the Endeavour
creator: Unknown illustrator
why_public_domain: Illustration from a Project Gutenberg edition of W.H.G. Kingston's "Captain Cook: His Life, Voyages and Discoveries". Kingston died in 1880, and the book first came out in 1871. Published before 1929.
original_holder: W.H.G. Kingston, Captain Cook: His Life, Voyages and Discoveries, via Project Gutenberg #24755
caption: The Endeavour, the ship that carried Cook, Charles Green and Joseph Banks to Tahiti to watch Venus cross the Sun on 3 June 1769.

title: William Herschel's 40-foot telescope
creator: Unknown engraver, after the 1795 plate in Philosophical Transactions
why_public_domain: An 18th-century instrument, shown in an engraving printed in 1893. Published before 1929.
original_holder: Oliver Lodge, Pioneers of Science (London: Macmillan, 1893), via Project Gutenberg #28613 (Fig. 83)
caption: Herschel's giant reflector at Slough, finished in 1789, was the largest telescope of its century. It shows how far observatory building went in the age of the Venus transits.

title: Venus on the Sun at the transit of 1874
creator: After a photograph by Jules Janssen
why_public_domain: Janssen's photograph dates from 1874, and this reproduction was printed in Robert Ball's The Story of the Heavens (revised edition, Cassell, c. 1897). Ball died in 1913. Published before 1929.
original_holder: Robert S. Ball, The Story of the Heavens, via Project Gutenberg #27378 (Fig. 45)
caption: The dark dot near the upper left is Venus crossing the face of the Sun in December 1874. The faint grid of lines on the plate was meant for measuring the planet's position.

title: Transit instrument for the British astronomical expedition, 1874
creator: Unknown engraver
why_public_domain: Engraving printed in 1893. Published before 1929, and the engraver is anonymous.
original_holder: Oliver Lodge, Pioneers of Science (London: Macmillan, 1893), via Project Gutenberg #28613 (Fig. 76)
caption: An observing hut built for the 1874 transit expeditions, with a transit telescope and a clock. Expeditions went worldwide to time Venus to the second.

title: Darwin's "I think" tree sketch, Notebook B

caption: In a private notebook in 1837, Darwin wrote "I think" and drew a branching tree: species splitting from common ancestors. It was the first sketch of a tree of life.

title: The divergence diagram from On the Origin of Species
creator: Charles Darwin
why_public_domain: Published in 1859. The author died in 1882.
original_holder: From On the Origin of Species (John Murray, 1859); image file from OpenStax Biology 2e, panel (a)

title: A. R. Wallace, Singapore, 1862
creator: Unknown photographer

title: A. R. Wallace soon after his return from the East
creator: Unknown photographer

original_holder: James Marchant, Alfred Russel Wallace: Letters and Reminiscences, Vol. 1, via Project Gutenberg #15997

original_holder: McClure's Magazine, Vol. 6 No. 5 (April 1896), via Project Gutenberg #14663

title: Radiograph made with the rays of radium

title: Photograph of various objects taken by means of pitchblende
